findings.highlight: it’d only end the conversation if I said that now
findings.evidenceJa: ここで注意しても話の腰を折るだけだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou withholds his objection because it would only derail or interrupt the discussion.
findings.explanation: The English makes his correction terminate the whole conversation, exaggerating the practical consequence.

findings.highlight: a devil lance that grows a thousand thorns once it stabs its enemy
findings.evidenceJa: 貫いた瞬間に内部から千の棘を生やして相手を絶命させる魔槍
findings.governingReading: One tradition describes a magical lance that sprouts a thousand thorns inside the pierced target and kills them.
findings.explanation: The English omits the lethal result that completes the cited tradition.

findings.highlight: in every one is the fact that it will always pierce the heart
findings.evidenceJa: その全てに“心臓を穿つ”という一節が残っている
findings.governingReading: Every version preserves a passage about piercing the heart.
findings.explanation: The English inserts “always” before Saber reaches her later conclusion about the weapon’s literal function, compressing the progression of her inference.

findings.highlight: It must be bending space or changing the order of cause and effect.
findings.evidenceJa: 空間をねじ曲げているのか、因果律を変えているのか
findings.governingReading: Saber weighs whether the lance bends space or alters causality.
findings.explanation: “Must be” turns two explicitly open possibilities into a firmer technical assertion.

findings.evidenceJa: こと一対一の戦闘において
findings.governingReading: The lance is extraordinarily efficient specifically in one-on-one combat.
findings.explanation: The English replaces a numerical engagement condition with combat range, losing the condition used again in page19.

findings.highlight: A servant with a rank A Noble Phantasm will need great amount of magical energy
findings.evidenceJa: Ａランクの宝具を持つ者は、その使用に大量の魔力を消費する
findings.governingReading: A Servant possessing an A-rank Noble Phantasm consumes a great amount of magical energy when using it.
findings.explanation: The English sentence lacks the required article and uses unstable title casing in a technical explanation.

findings.highlight: a Servant who’s not flashy, but can definitely win
findings.evidenceJa: 堅実に勝利を収められるサーヴァント
findings.governingReading: Shirou characterizes Lancer as unflashy but capable of securing victories reliably.
findings.explanation: “Definitely win” converts tactical reliability into an unconditional victory guarantee.

findings.highlight: He was heartless, but he also had a side that was difficult to hate.
findings.evidenceJa: 非情な人物ではありましたが、どこか憎めない一面がありました
findings.governingReading: Saber finds Lancer ruthless, yet possessing a side one cannot quite hate.
findings.explanation: “Heartless” shifts a judgment about merciless conduct into a broader claim about his emotional nature.

findings.highlight: He stabbed me through heart as if he was cutting grass.
findings.evidenceJa: アイツは草を刈るような気軽さで俺の心臓を貫いた
findings.governingReading: Lancer pierced Shirou’s heart with the casual ease of cutting grass.
findings.explanation: The missing article produces malformed English at the scene’s reminder of Lancer’s lethal ease.
